name: North Macedonia
description:
A landlocked Balkan nation with ancient history, picturesque lake towns, and a very low cost of living in Europe. Known for low taxes and a new nomad program.

## Key Highlights
- Ancient towns and spectacular lake scenery in UNESCO-listed Ohrid
- Extremely low flat 10% income tax and 10% corporate tax rates
- Very low cost of living compared to Western European countries
longdescription: North Macedonia is a landlocked country in the Balkan Peninsula, bordered by Greece, Albania, Kosovo, Serbia, and Bulgaria. With a population of 2 million, it features a unique blend of Ottoman, Mediterranean, and European influences. The capital, Skopje, is known for its historic Old Bazaar alongside contemporary grand neoclassical monuments and bridges. North Macedonia offers a rich history, beautiful mountain ranges, and stunning lakes, particularly Lake Ohrid, one of Europe's oldest and deepest lakes. The country has a very low cost of living, making it highly attractive to digital nomads and retirees seeking affordable European living. North Macedonia is business-friendly, offering a flat 10% tax rate on personal and corporate income. The government is currently developing a digital nomad visa program to attract remote workers.

visas.name: North Macedonia Company Registration Residence
visas.description: A temporary residence permit granted to foreign nationals who register an LLC company in North Macedonia and employ themselves, with a minimal share capital requirement.
benefits: Low operating and corporate tax costs (10%)
visas.path_to_residency_description: Can apply for permanent residency after 5 years of continuous temporary residence.

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Acquired if born to at least one citizen of North Macedonia at the time of birth.

Naturalization.desc:
**Requirements:** 8 years continuous legal residence (permanent residency status), basic knowledge of Macedonian language, clean criminal record, renunciation of other citizenships.

**Dual citizenship:** Permitted under specific conditions, particularly for ethnic Macedonians or investors.

tax_advice:
- Flat 10% personal income tax rate
- Flat 10% corporate income tax rate
- Standard Value Added Tax (VAT) rate is 18% (reduced rate of 5% on food/utilities)
- Capital gains tax is flat 10%
- Property tax ranges from 0.1% to 0.2% annually
- Double tax treaties exist with over 45 countries, including Germany, the UK, and France
local_tips:
- Macedonian is the official language; English is spoken by younger generations in Skopje and Ohrid, but limited in government offices
- Cash is widely used; Macedonian Denar (MKD) is the currency and card payments are accepted in major supermarkets
- Healthcare: public system is basic; private healthcare (e.g. Acibadem Sistina) is recommended
- Cost of living is low; budget €800-1,200/month for a high-quality lifestyle
- Internet is fast and reliable in major cities via VDSL or cable, with 5G expanding
